name: Modified artificial seawater (ASW) medium, P-free base + P source as indicated (PMC10132767)
description: Modified artificial seawater (ASW) medium, P-free base + P source as indicated — medium reported in PMC10132767, extracted for GrowthDB and mapped to BiGG.

provenance.citation: Medium composition from PMC10132767 (see GrowthDB record).
provenance.notes: Composition mapped to BiGG (mapper + salt dissociation); presence-based bounds; paper_amount retained. Added via GrowthDB curation.
provenance.verification: paper-verified (complete recipe; cited + supplementary sources chased)
provenance.verification_evidence: ASW medium (Wilson et al. 1996) media-comparison table, ASW column: 'NaCl ... 25' g/L (footnote 5 Wilson et al. (1996) J. Phycol 32, 506-516)
provenance.base_medium: Artificial seawater (ASW) medium of Wilson, Carr & Mann 1996 (J. Phycol. 32:506-516), modified: NaNO3 replaced by 8.8 mM NH4Cl, 10 mM sodium succinate added as carbon source, MAMS vitamins (Chen 2012) added at 1 ml/L, and P reduced/varied (50 uM-1.73 mM) supplied as K2HPO4, phosphocholine or phosphorylethanolamine.

sources_chased.what: base ASW recipe cited as ref 61 (Wilson, Carr & Mann 1996, J. Phycol. 32:506-516)
sources_chased.how: WebFetch/Read of the Chisholm-lab (MIT) Prochlorococcus & Synechococcus culturing manual media-comparison table, whose ASW column is explicitly footnoted 'Wilson et al. (1996) J. Phycol 32, 506-516'

sources_chased.what: MAMS vitamins solution cited as ref 62 (Chen 2012, Environ. Microbiol. 14:2308-2322)
sources_chased.how: WebFetch of marine-Roseobacter methods (PMC8319176 and DSMZ medium 1313 / PMC4331573) that reproduce the Chen-2012 MAMS medium and its 1 ml/L vitamin solution

recuration.notes: Base is the Wilson-Carr-Mann 1996 ASW; the paper modifies it by supplying carbon (10 mM Na-succinate), N as 8.8 mM NH4Cl (equimolar substitution for the base ASW's 8.8 mM NaNO3, so nitrate is treated as replaced) and vitamins via 1 ml/L MAMS solution. P is the experimental variable (50 uM-1.73 mM) supplied as K2HPO4, phosphocholine (PC) or phosphorylethanolamine (PE), with a -P control. Grown aerobically (30 C, shaking); no reductant/anaerobic gas. Mo and B trace metals and all nine MAMS vitamins were absent from the prior component list and are the main recovered additions; hydrate forms for

components.mapping_note: [CHEM-B12-01] cbl1 is Cob(I)alamin, the transient reduced Co(I) intracellular redox state of the cofactor -- it is not a dietary or medium B12 species. Cyanocobalamin (C63H88CoN14O14P) has no in_biggr BiGG id (b12 carries no formula and no InChIKey and is absent from BiGGr). adocbl (Adenosylcobalamin, C72H100CoN18O17P, ZIHHMGTYZOSFRC-QRVZQHAISA-N) is a real dietary/coenzyme B12 form present in BiGGr and is recorded as a declared proxy for the vitamer group, not as an exact identity.
